description: The system shall implement policies and procedures that review a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process based on the organization’s access authorization policies.

description: The system shall implement policies and procedures that modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process based on the organization’s access authorization policies.
LLM_reasoning: Central audit trail via TransactionLogger/TransactionDAO; patients can review via ViewMyAccessLogAction
GT_reasoning: The application does not provide a way to modify that user’s access or role or disable the account. The only in-app changes that affect access are contextual assignments (e.g., hospital/ward assignments, declared HCPs per patient), which determine where and for whom a user operates. However, the system does not provide robust policy or approval workflows for these actions; instead, it relies on personnel to manually modify authorization decisions.

description: The system must allow individuals to request an amendment to their protected health information maintained in designated record sets, for as long as the information is retained in those sets.

GT_reasoning: The requirement expects a mechanism that allows an individual to submit a request to amend PHI in designated record sets. Patients can directly edit some of their own data. But there is no page that lets a patient file a formal request to amend my record.

description: The system may allow a covered entity to obtain an individual’s consent to use or disclose protected health information for treatment operations.
LLM_reasoning: No workflow to capture consent for treatment use; privacyPolicy.jsp states implicit use only
GT_reasoning: Patients (or personal representatives) fill out a “Medical records release form” to authorize disclosure of their medical records to a named doctor and hospital. Then this consent is converted into a formal release request record through verifying the digital signature matches the logged-in name. Then HCPs/UAPs view pending release requests. Once approved, a “Download Medical Records” link appears, which invokes RecordsReleaseXMLServlet to export the patient’s medical records for that specific, consented release.

description: The system may allow a covered entity to obtain an individual’s consent to use or disclose protected health information for payment operations.
LLM_reasoning: No consent capture for payment; only billing views without consent
GT_reasoning: There is no dedicated mechanism to obtain an individual’s consent for payment operations

description: The system may allow a covered entity to obtain an individual’s consent to use or disclose protected health information for health care operations.

GT_reasoning: web.xml grants HCP role access to treatment pages (/auth/hcp/*) and PHI of the patients, enabling treatment operations.

description: The system shall ensure the integrity of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it receives.
LLM_reasoning: No technical integrity controls for received ePHI
GT_reasoning: Received ePHI is submitted via uploadPatientFile.jsp, which is a personnel function; So HCP and UAP ensure integrity of ePHI while entering it on the server.

description: The system shall ensure the integrity of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it maintains.
LLM_reasoning: No technical integrity controls for maintained ePHI
GT_reasoning: The system does not implement integrity mechanisms on stored data (e.g. hashes or signatures on records) to detect tampering outside the application (e.g. direct DB changes). Integrity is only supported by access control and authorization, but not by cryptographic or storage-level integrity checks.

description: The system shall implement procedures for guarding against malicious software.
LLM_reasoning: No code or procedures for guarding against malware; searches show only medical virus codes
GT_reasoning: The system has no malware-specific safeguards (no antivirus, no file scanning). It implements procedures that reduce the impact of malicious input, which can be considered partial “guarding” against malicious behavior. (1) Many JSPs use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml() when outputting user input to help guard against script injection in the browser. However, it is not enforced across the entire codebase. For example, Review text is user-generated, and output without escaping is a direct XSS risk.  Also, appointment comments are stored and displayed without escaping. (2) DAOs use PreparedStatement for database access, so user input is parameterized and not concatenated into SQL, reducing SQL injection risk. (3) Validators and ValidationFormat reject invalid input. (4) The only upload (patient CSV) is parsed as CSV, so the app does not blindly accept arbitrary files.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices includes a statement that the covered entity is required to follow the terms of the notice currently in effect.
LLM_reasoning: No commitment to follow the notice currently in effect
GT_reasoning: The privacy policy contains no statement that the covered entity is required to follow the terms of the notice currently in effect.

description: The system shall support implementing security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with the general security requirements.
LLM_reasoning: Security controls exist but patient selection trusts UID_PATIENTID from request without authorization
GT_reasoning: The system implements a baseline of security measures, role-based access control, salted password hashing, login-failure throttling, and session timeout. However, it falls short of reasonable and appropriate because ePHI is stored in plaintext (no encryption at rest), there are no backup/recovery procedures, and XSS protection is inconsistently applied.

description: The system shall support procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, including audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.

GT_reasoning: The system provides audit logs and access reports for review, but it does not implement security-incident tracking reports. It also doesn't enforce regular reviewing.

GT_reasoning: The Access/Participation section states: The privacy policy requires us to allow you access to your medical records, which partially addresses inspection and access.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices informs individuals of their right to request an amendment to their protected health information.

GT_reasoning: The Access/Participation section states: Please contact the iTrust System Administrator or your medical professional if you feel any information is incorrect or needs to be changed, which implies a right to amendment but never explicitly frames it as a formal right.

description: The system shall support conducting an accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the integrity of electronic protected health information (ePHI)
LLM_reasoning: Audit trail provides traceability; but no explicit risk/vulnerability assessment process or integrity checking
GT_reasoning: The system does not implement any explicit risk assessment mechanism for assessing the integrity.

description: The system must ensure that each description of permitted or required use or disclosure includes sufficient detail to notify the individual of how their information may be used or disclosed.

GT_reasoning: The privacy policy contains no mention of how the information will be used or disclosed.

description: The system must ensure that the notice of privacy practices describes the types of uses and disclosures that require written authorization, includes a statement that any other uses or disclosures will only be made with written authorization, and informs the individual of their right to revoke that authorization.

GT_reasoning: The policy only vaguely mentions written authorization for disclosures outside the listed permitted categories, but never describes the specific types of uses or disclosures that require it. There is also no mention of the individual's right to revoke authorization.

GT_reasoning: The system does not consistently apply minimum necessary when retrieving PHI. Several flows load full patient records when only one or two fields are needed.

description: The system shall ensure the availability of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it creates.
LLM_reasoning: Data stored with audit log; availability depends on single MyISAM instance with no backup/HA
GT_reasoning: Created ePHI is written to the database, and once the transaction commits, it is available for later reads. The application does not implement backup or recovery of created data. So, in the event of database or storage loss or corruption, that data would be unavailable or lost.

description: The system shall ensure the availability of all electronic protected health information (ePHI) that it receives.
LLM_reasoning: Incoming ePHI stored in MyISAM tables; no replication/ACID/backup or disaster recovery
GT_reasoning: Transmission of ePHI only occurs when the user can load pages that include authenticate.jsp; that logic returns 503 when the database is unavailable, so the application does not attempt to transmit ePHI when it cannot reliably read or serve it.
